brief: GS's trading floor describes a quiet close to a hectic week: LOs and HFs finished moderate net sellers, with supply most acute in tech. Aggregate net TMT (Info Tech + Comm Services) selling has reached ~$20bn over two weeks, approaching the -$23bn seen in July's AI selling episode. Mood remains terrible and performance challenges persist. Unlike last week, there was almost no rotation out of AI into defensives despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and pockets of Financials, and zero offensive positioning around AI all week. US equities were net sold a third straight week (4 of last 5), driven by Single Stock long/short sales in the largest de-grossing since late July; Industrials was sold at the fastest HF pace in 6+ months while Real Estate and Staples were bought, reinforcing a defensive posture. Gross leverage rose to 216.1% (64th percentile, 1yr) while Net leverage fell to 43.4% (0th percentile, 5yr). Next week: S&P implied move of 1.80% into FOMC/BOC, ECB, BOJ decisions, the heaviest Q3 earnings week (44% of S&P cap), and Brazil's election.
